title: An entity browser
description:
Combine the milestone into the model behind a real tool window: a table of entities with a filter box, sortable columns, multi-selection and a clipped, scrolling body.

```cpp
struct Entity { int id; std::string name; std::string team; int hp; };
struct SortSpec { int column; bool ascending; };   // 0 name, 1 team, 2 hp

class EntityBrowser
{
public:
    explicit EntityBrowser(std::vector<Entity> entities);
    void setFilter(const std::string& filter);                       // lesson 2.03's word matching on name and team
    void setSort(const std::vector<SortSpec>& specs);                 // lesson 3.03
    std::vector<int> rows() const;                                    // ids of visible entities, filtered and sorted
    void click(int id, bool ctrl, bool shift);                        // lesson 3.04's rules over rows()
    std::vector<int> selected() const;                                // sorted ids
    std::vector<int> visibleRows(float scrollY, float viewHeight, float rowHeight) const;   // lesson 3.02, ids
    void removeSelected();                                            // deletes the selected entities
    int count() const;                                                // entities left
};
```

Rules:

- `rows()` holds the entities whose **name or team** match the filter, sorted by the specs (stable; with no specs, in the original order).
- The **selection is by id** and survives filtering and sorting. Selected entities that the filter hides stay selected.
- `click` uses the current `rows()` as display order for Shift ranges.
- `visibleRows` returns the ids of the rows the clipper would draw for that scroll position.
- `removeSelected` deletes every selected entity, including hidden ones, and clears the selection and the anchor.
hints: `rows()` does filtering then sorting every time it is called, from the full list. Selection only ever stores ids, so nothing needs updating when the filter or sort changes.
requirements: Filtering, sorting and selection can be combined in any order.
The selection is kept by id across filter and sort changes.
Only the rows on screen are reported for drawing.
Deleting removes exactly the selected entities.
stretch: Cache `rows()` and rebuild it only when the filter, the sort or the data changes, like a real tool does when the table has 50,000 rows.
